stem: Which combination of findings places a hospitalized client at increased risk for pressure injury?

options.A: Independent mobility, intact sensory perception, adequate nutrition, and skin that is rarely exposed to moisture.
options.B: Frequent ambulation, intact sensation, adequate food intake, and ability to reposition without assistance throughout the day.
options.C: Independent repositioning, preserved sensory perception, adequate nutrition, and little friction or shear during movement.
options.D: Limited mobility, impaired sensory perception, poor nutritional intake, and skin that is frequently or persistently moist.

rationale: The July 2026 StatPearls/NCBI update describes pressure-injury risk as multifactorial and identifies impaired mobility, poor nutrition, and impaired sensation among major risk factors. It also describes the Braden scale domains of sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition, and friction/shear; greater moisture exposure and impairment in these domains increase risk. Therefore D combines several established risk factors. A, B, and C instead describe protective or lower-risk characteristics.
educational_objective: Recognize impaired mobility, impaired sensory perception, poor nutrition, and frequent moisture exposure as major pressure-injury risk factors.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf) / StatPearls
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; last update July 5, 2026; live NCBI page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Etiology/History and Physical: decreased mobility, malnutrition, sensory impairment and related comorbidities increase risk. History and Physical/Evaluation: Braden scale evaluates sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition, and friction/shear; higher impairment/moisture exposure corresponds to greater risk.
source_claim_supported: Pressure-injury risk rises with impaired mobility and sensation, poor nutrition, and adverse moisture exposure; these domains are incorporated into Braden assessment.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — identify risk factors and prevent complications.
correction_summary: Balanced option lengths and made each alternative a parallel combination of mobility, sensory, nutrition, and skin-moisture characteristics.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — current NCBI guidance and Braden domains directly support all four risk elements in D; the other choices describe lower-risk profiles.
